edges.description: Poorly deformable red cells are removed from the circulation, giving chronic hemolysis.
Chronic red-cell destruction produces the hemolytic anemia.
Splenic clearance of abnormal red cells enlarges the spleen.

Iron accumulates over the disease course; the route is not established in the KCNN4 form (see the Iron Overload Mechanism knowledge gap), so this edge records the clinical association rather than a resolved mechanism.

nodes.description: The trigger lesion. The Gardos channel is a calcium-activated, potassium-selective channel in the red-cell membrane that participates in cell-volume regulation. Gain-of-function KCNN4 variants increase the channel's calcium sensitivity, so it opens at lower intracellular calcium concentrations than the wild-type channel; red-cell Ca2+ overload has also been observed in patient erythrocytes.

nodes.description: Potassium efflux through the over-active Gardos channel produces a red-cell cation leak (elevated sodium, reduced potassium) and dysregulated cell volume. In the accepted model the cell loses water and dehydrates (xerocytosis), and that is the picture in the discovery kindreds; but the hydration endpoint is variant-dependent. The recurrent R352H allele shows compensatory ion-transport changes that prevent frank dehydration (with Ca2+ overload instead), and the V222L and H340N variants show no obvious dehydration, so the dehydration step is the conventional model rather than an obligate consequence (see the Variable Dehydration knowledge gap).
